## Loading libraries
```{r}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(kableExtra)
```


## Loading data
```{r}
#| output: false
coralnet <- read.csv(here("Week_8", "Data", "annotations.csv"))
head(coralnet)

labelset <- read.csv(here("Week_8", "Data", "CoralNet_Labelset.csv"))

```


## Data analysis

### Function 1: Benthic Cover Summary Table

My first goal is to make a function that can read in a CoralNet output .csv and generate a clear summary output table of benthic cover with broader functional group categories.

First, I'm writing the code to do what I want on a small subset of data (only two photoquad outputs):
```{r}
#| output: false
twoquads <- head(coralnet, 100)
glimpse(twoquads)
tail(twoquads)
#starting by looking only at quadrat C and E and from 11/11/25 
```

Writing code to data wrangle and summarize to make a clean summary kable table:
```{r}
summary_table <- twoquads %>%
  left_join(labelset, by = "Label.code") %>%
  filter(!Label.code %in% c("OOQ","PVC","UNK","MOBL")) %>% #filtering out points that are unknown, outside quadrat, mobile fauna, or on PVC (not included in % cover calculations)
  group_by(Name) %>%
  mutate(Total.points = n()) %>% #calculating the total number of points included per quadrat for benthic cover calculations
  group_by(Date, Site, GoPro.ID, Functional.group, ID.Name, Total.points) %>%
  summarise(Point.count = n()) %>%
  mutate(Percent.cover = round((Point.count / Total.points) * 100, 2)) %>% #converting point count to percent cover, rounding to 2 decimal places 
  select(!c(Total.points, Point.count)) %>%
  kbl(col.names = c('Date', 'Site', 'Quadrat', 'Functional Group', 'Benthic ID', 'Percent Cover (%)')) %>%
  collapse_rows(columns = 1:4, #collapsing/collecting rows that are the same in columns 1-4 (will be repeated for multiple rows so don't want to re-print)
                target = 3, #collapsing by quadrat ID column, so that it still prints date and site for each quadrat
                valig = "top") #aligning collapsed text to the top 
summary_table
```
*Note: For my purposes, it makes sense to keep each quadrat summarized separately, since each quadrat corresponds to a paired video behavioral assay. For broader purposes / future directions, I could also take this a step farther to average across all quadrats for each site and day.*

**Making my code into a function that can be used more broadly:**
```{r}

benthic_table <- function(data, labelset, exclude_codes = c("OOQ", "PVC", "UNK", "MOBL")) { #these exclude codes can be changed based on specific project / investigation
  data %>%
    left_join(labelset, by = "Label.code") %>%
    filter(!Label.code %in% exclude_codes) %>% #filtering out points that are in pre-defined exclude codes: for my purposes, unknown, outside quadrat, or on PVC
    group_by(Name) %>%
    mutate(Total.points = n()) %>% #calculating the total number of points included per quadrat for benthic cover calculations
    group_by(Date, Site, GoPro.ID, Functional.group, ID.Name, Total.points) %>%
    summarise(Point.count = n()) %>%
    mutate(Percent.cover = round((Point.count / Total.points) * 100, 2)) %>% #converting point count to percent cover, rounding to 2 decimal places 
    select(!c(Total.points, Point.count)) %>%
    kbl(col.names = c('Date', 'Site', 'Quadrat', 'Functional Group', 'Benthic ID', 'Percent Cover (%)')) %>%
    collapse_rows(columns = 1:4, #collapsing/collecting rows that are the same in columns 1-4 (will be repeated for multiple rows so don't want to re-print)
                target = 3, #collapsing by quadrat ID column, so that it still prints date and site for each quadrat
                valig = "top") #aligning collapsed text to the top 
}
```

Testing, on my smaller dataframe w/ 2 quadrats and then with a fuller dataset:
```{r}
#two quadrats
benthic_table(twoquads, labelset)

#fuller dataset
benthic_table(coralnet, labelset)
```

### Function 2: Stacked barplot of benthic cover

Now, I want to create a function that will make a summary barplot of the benthic cover categories. First, I'll write the code to accomplish this.

```{r}
#data wrangling to get summarized data
summarized_data <- twoquads %>%
  left_join(labelset, by = "Label.code") %>%
  filter(!Label.code %in% c("OOQ","PVC","UNK","MOBL")) %>% #filtering out points that are unknown, outside quadrat, mobile fauna, or on PVC (not included in % cover calculations)
  group_by(Name) %>%
  mutate(Total.points = n()) %>% #calculating the total number of points included per quadrat for benthic cover calculations
  group_by(Date, Site, GoPro.ID, Subcategory, Label.code, ID.Name, Total.points) %>%
  summarise(Point.count = n()) %>%
  mutate(Percent.cover = round((Point.count / Total.points) * 100, 2)) #converting point count to percent cover, rounding to 2 decimal places
```

```{r}
#making benthic color palette, that makes sense biologically for the groups that they're encoding
benthic_pal <- c(
  "Coral" = "#C0504D",
  "CCA" = "#F4C2C2",
  "Macroalgae" = "#0F3800",
  "Turf" = "#16A34A",
  "Sand" = "#E8D8B0",
  "Urchin" = "#5E50A1",
  "Other Invertebrates" = "#0096C7",
  "Cyanobacteria" = "#5C1A48"
)
```


```{r}
ggplot(summarized_data, aes(x=GoPro.ID, y=Percent.cover, fill=Subcategory))+
  geom_col()+
  geom_text( #adding text to plot the % turf cover (the highest cover across my quadrats, important for me because I'm relating these plots to grazing rates)
    data = summarized_data %>%
      group_by(Site, Date, GoPro.ID) %>%
      filter(Subcategory == "Turf") %>% #filtering for the multiple label codes that are all more broadly classified as turf
      summarise(Total.turf = sum(Percent.cover), .groups = "drop"), #getting a value for the total turf for each quadrat
    aes(x = GoPro.ID, 
      y = Total.turf / 2, #positions the turf % label in the middle of the combined turf chunk
      label = paste0(round(Total.turf), "%")
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, #prevents ggplot from looking for 'Subcategory' in this geom text layer
    color = "white", size = 3, fontface = "bold") + #changing text font size/color + bolding
  scale_fill_manual(values = benthic_pal)+ #changing colors to pre-defined benthic color palette
  facet_wrap(~ Site + Date, scales = "free_x", strip.position = "bottom") +
  labs(x = "Quadrat",
    y = "Percent Cover",
    fill = "Benthic Category",
    title = "Benthic Cover by Quadrat"
  )+
  theme_minimal()
```
*For the code above, I also printed the total turf cover (important for me because I'm relating these benthic cover plots to herbivorous fish grazing), but for the function below, I got rid of this to make the figure simpler/more versatile.*


**Now, making the above chunks into a function:**
```{r}
benthic_plot <- function(benthicdata, labelset, exclude_codes = c("OOQ", "PVC", "UNK", "MOBL")) {
  
  benthic_pal <- c(
  "Coral" = "#C0504D",
  "CCA" = "#F4C2C2",
  "Macroalgae" = "#0F3800",
  "Turf" = "#16A34A",
  "Sand" = "#E8D8B0",
  "Urchin" = "#5E50A1",
  "Other Invertebrates" = "#0096C7",
  "Cyanobacteria" = "#5C1A48"
)
  
  benthicdata %>%
    left_join(labelset, by = "Label.code") %>%
    filter(!Label.code %in% exclude_codes) %>% #filtering out points that are in pre-defined exclude codes: for my purposes, unknown, outside quadrat, or on PVC
    group_by(Name) %>%
    mutate(Total.points = n()) %>% #calculating the total number of points included per quadrat for benthic cover calculations
    group_by(Date, Site, GoPro.ID, Subcategory, Label.code, ID.Name, Total.points) %>%
    summarise(Point.count = n()) %>%
    mutate(Percent.cover = round((Point.count / Total.points) * 100, 2)) %>%
    
    ggplot(aes(x=GoPro.ID, y=Percent.cover, fill=Subcategory))+
    geom_col()+
    scale_fill_manual(values = benthic_pal)+ #changing colors to pre-defined benthic color palette
    facet_wrap(~ Site + Date, scales = "free_x", strip.position = "bottom") +
    labs(x = "Quadrat",
         y = "Percent Cover",
         fill = "Benthic Category",
         title = "Benthic Cover by Quadrat"
         )+
    theme_minimal()
}
```

Testing my new function, with smaller 2-quadrat subset and then with fuller dataset:
```{r}
#two quadrats
benthic_plot(twoquads, labelset)

#fuller datset
benthic_plot(coralnet, labelset)
```
